public_rationale: Read plainly, the claim says the big, well-funded AI players spend their money on scaling rather than on a test like the comprehension challenge. In January 2025, OpenAI and its partners announced up to $500 billion for compute, and OpenAI said the compute would train leading models. Microsoft said it would spend over $80 billion on AI data centers in fiscal 2025. Next to these sums, a $25-50 million test is tiny, and no search turned up any lab paying for a full version of it. The evidence supports the general claim. But it rests on a reading of 'prefer' as where money goes, and on data-center spending standing in for research budgets.
limitations: Interpretive: 'prefer' and 'research dollars' are loose terms.
Relies on news reports; the OpenAI primary announcement could not be read (HTTP 403).
Labs also spend on safety, evaluations and other research that this evidence does not measure.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Those who could afford to build the comprehension challenge prefer to spend research money on scaling.

statement.excerpt: The people who could afford it prefer to put their research dollars in scaling.
statement.document_title: AI has (sort of) passed the Turing Test; here’s why that hardly matters

from_speaker: The people who could afford it
prefer to put their research dollars in scaling
contrast with a $25 or $50 million comprehension-challenge effort
our_interpretation: Plain reading: the well-funded AI developers (OpenAI and peers) direct their money mainly to scaling, meaning more compute and bigger models, and have not paid for a full comprehension-challenge test.
'Prefer' is read as revealed preference shown by where spending goes, not as a claim about inner motives.
No period is named, so the claim is read as describing the state just before the post: roughly January 2025 to the post date, 2025-04-02.
This is a qualitative claim about research priorities with no figure, so metric_scope is left null; spending announcements are used as evidence of direction, not to check a number.
criteria.support_condition: Public reports from the period show the major well-funded AI developers committing very large sums to compute and data-center scaling, with no sign that any of them funded a full comprehension-challenge test.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that well-funded labs put a major share of their research money into non-scaling work such as large evaluation efforts, or that one of them funded a full comprehension challenge of the kind described.
